properties.name: Central District
properties.description: Northern metropolitan zone and Barossa Valley country pipeline before the introduction of the AFL national draft.
properties.famous_players: John Platten, Greg Edwards, Peter Vivian
properties.trivia: Central District was South Australia's working-class powerhouse, producing Magarey Medallist John Platten before his move to Hawthorn.

properties.name: Glenelg
properties.description: Brighton and Holdfast Bay coast alongside the prolific South East recruitment zone.
properties.famous_players: Stephen Kernahan, Peter Maynard, Stephen Copping, Tony McGuinness
properties.trivia: Graham Cornes led Glenelg to back-to-back flags in 1985 and 1986 with a team stacked with South East country recruits.

properties.name: North Adelaide
properties.description: Prospect corridor and Spencer Gulf country recruiting grounds.
properties.famous_players: Barrie Robran, Darren Jarman, Andrew Jarman, Mick Redden
properties.trivia: North Adelaide won the 1987 SANFL Premiership under Michael Nunan, executing an innovative running handball game.

properties.name: Norwood
properties.description: Eastern suburbs and Eyre Peninsula territory.
properties.famous_players: Michael Aish, Craig Balme, Garry McIntosh, Neville Roberts
properties.trivia: In 1984, Bob Hammond's Norwood Redlegs became the 'History Makers', winning four consecutive finals from fifth to claim the flag.

properties.name: Port Adelaide
properties.description: Historic Alberton/Port Adelaide docks and Western Eyre Peninsula recruitment.
properties.famous_players: Russell Ebert, Greg Phillips, Tim Ginever, Stephen Williams
properties.trivia: John Cahill led Port Adelaide to premierships in 1988, 1989, and 1990 immediately prior to the birth of the Adelaide Crows.

properties.name: South Adelaide
properties.description: Southern metropolitan and Fleurieu/Kangaroo Island zones.
properties.famous_players: Rick Davies, Mark Bickley, David Kappler
properties.trivia: Rick Davies kicked 151 goals for South Adelaide in 1983, a legendary individual performance in SANFL history.

properties.name: Sturt
properties.description: Unley, Mitcham hills foothills, and Murraylands country zone.
properties.famous_players: Paul Bagshaw, Michael Graham, Tony Burgan, Bruce Winter
properties.trivia: The Double Blues won five straight SANFL premierships (1966–1970) under Jack Oatey, setting a benchmark for team discipline.

properties.name: West Adelaide
properties.description: Inner-west Adelaide and Riverland agricultural belt.
properties.famous_players: Mark Mickan, Brian Leys, Bruce Lindner, Leon Gross
properties.trivia: Neil Kerley's 1983 premiership side was dubbed the 'Kerley's Heroes', toppling Sturt in a famous Grand Final triumph.

properties.name: Woodville
properties.description: North of Port Road & Grange Road (Woodville, Cheltenham, Findon, Seaton, Grange) plus Northern Yorke Peninsula (Kadina, Wallaroo, Moonta, Bute).
properties.famous_players: Malcolm Blight, Ralph Sewer, Colin Parker, Allen Greer
properties.trivia: Home of Australian Football Hall of Fame Legend Malcolm Blight, who kicked 126 goals for the Warriors in 1985 before their 1991 merger.

properties.name: West Torrens
properties.description: South of Port Road & Grange Road (Thebarton, Torrensville, Mile End, Lockleys, Fulham, West Beach) plus Southern Yorke Peninsula (Maitland, Minlaton, Yorketown, Edithburgh).
properties.famous_players: Bob Hank, Lindsay Head, Neville Roberts, Fred Bills
properties.trivia: Foundation SANFL club famous for dual Magarey Medallists Bob Hank and Lindsay Head. The Eagles played at Thebarton Oval from 1922 until merging with Woodville.
